findings.title: Emerging Threat: Optimizely and Three Other Providers Poisoned in iOS Exploit and Skimming Campaign
findings.summary_md: Beazley Security reported malicious JavaScript in Optimizely Web Experimentation customer project files served from cdn.optimizely.com, with the same campaign also reaching scripts from Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly. The advisory describes a cryptocurrency address swapper, payment card skimmer, cookie and screenshot exfiltration, and iOS stages linked to Coruna and DarkSword delivery infrastructure. It says the earliest observations for the other providers date to November 13, three days before the Optimizely reports, and that Optimizely had published no statement, root cause or remediation guidance. It recommends checking the served project file, removing snippets from sensitive pages, blocking 1688360.cc and named .icu hosts in CSP, and treating first-party card fields as possible card data exposure.

findings.title: CNN, Zoom, Fox News Served Visitors a Crypto-Stealing Skimmer - OPTIMJACK (Nov 2026)
findings.summary_md: Amirul Cyber documented 15 page loads on household-name sites whose Optimizely bundles fetched 1688360.cc/track.js, including cdn.optimizely.com/js/5113954737848320.js on about.gitlab.com. The write-up breaks the payload into a checksum-validating crypto clipper covering eight chains, a screenshot and cookie exfiltration module posting to /hit.php, a card skimmer using Luhn checks and sendBeacon to /card.php, and an iOS second stage from two .icu hosts. It records that two sites blocked the payload through CSP script-src while the poisoned snippet still loaded, and lists IOCs including the SHA-256 of track.js and attacker wallet addresses.

findings.title: Bright.nl, VI.nl en andere websites verspreidden iPhone-malware via advertenties
findings.summary_md: Tweakers reported that Bright.nl, VI.nl and other Dutch websites warned they had unknowingly distributed malicious code through a hacked advertising system in early November. The code collected visitor information and attempted to exploit outdated iPhones, with GeenStijl identifying the payload as Coruna. The affected publishers said the code was removed and the advertising-system vulnerability fixed. This was a separate advertising compromise from the Optimizely incident, but it is the earliest public Coruna delivery reporting cited alongside it.
